context_tags: [hf, gdmt, EF]

Pharmacological management of heart failure with reduced ejection fraction.
In patients with symptomatic HFrEF, defined as EF below 40 percent on
echocardiography or cardiac MR, the recommendation is initiation of
guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT) comprising an ARNI or ACE
inhibitor, a beta-blocker, an MRA, and an SGLT2 inhibitor, titrated to the
maximally tolerated doses (Class I). A reduced EF on cardiac MR or
echocardiography should trigger GDMT initiation as early as possible after
diagnosis, provided hemodynamic stability. Reassessment of EF after three to
six months of optimized GDMT guides continued management. Patients whose EF
remains below 40 percent despite therapy should be evaluated for device
therapy. This management recommendation is a Class I indication.
